sections.label: Flat local employment growth
sections.summary: Local employment grew by a net 500 over 18 months, with unemployment reaching 3% in June 2016, due to slower local workforce growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: In response to Mr Patrick Tay and Mr Melvin Yong, on the ground, there is much concern that local employment growth has been flat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: It went up by 700 last year and came down by 200 in the first half of this year, giving a net increase of just 500 over 18 months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Fortunately, while the unemployment rate has increased, it did not rise sharply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: It exceeded marginally the range of 2.6% - 2.9% registered in the past five years, to reach 3% in June 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: With the help of my colleagues at MOM, I soon discovered that the main reason for the flat growth in local employment was a slowdown in local workforce growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: In the three years from 2012 to 2014, an average of 226,000 locals joined and 153,000 left the workforce each year, giving an average net increase of 73,000, or 79,000 if we were to include the self-employed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: But in 2015, the number of locals entering dropped significantly by about 36,000, while the number leaving increased by about 37,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: This is a swing of 73,000 and resulted in the flat growth in our local employment to just 700.

sections.label: Foreign manpower increase drop
sections.summary: The annual increase in foreign manpower fell by more than two-thirds, from 80,000 in 2011 to about 24,000 in the past two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: In response to Mr Liang Eng Hwa and Ms Foo Mee Har, the annual increase in foreign manpower has dropped significantly by more than two-thirds, from the last peak of 80,000 in 2011 to about 24,000 in the past two years.

sections.label: Concern over higher layoffs
sections.summary: The speaker shares concern that layoffs could be higher than before, especially in sectors facing weak demand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: In response to Mr Desmond Choo and Mr Liang Eng Hwa, we share their concern that we could see a higher number of layoffs than before, especially in sectors facing weak demand.

sections.label: Jobseekers assisted and placed
sections.summary: In the first eight months, Workforce Singapore and e2i assisted 20,000 jobseekers, with over 13,000 finding jobs across various sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: In the first eight months of this year, Workforce Singapore and e2i have assisted 20,000 active jobseekers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: More than 13,000 of them managed to find jobs in various sectors, including Infocomm Technology, Healthcare, Early Childhood Care and Education, Professional Services, Admin and Support, Biologics Manufacturing, Transport and Logistics, just to name the key ones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: For the PMETs, the number of PMETs who managed to secure jobs with our employment support went up by 45%; for the rank-and-file workers, it went up by 12%.

sections.label: New Professional Conversion Programmes
sections.summary: 24 new Professional Conversion Programmes were rolled out this year across 14 sectors, including International Trade and Cybersecurity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: In response to Mr Melvin Yong, we rolled out 24 new Professional Conversion Programmes (PCPs) this year in 14 sectors, such as International Trade and Cybersecurity.

sections.label: Retrenched locals who were PMETs
sections.summary: In the first half of this year, about 4,000 of the 5,700 retrenched locals were PMETs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: In fact, in the first half of this year, of the 5,700 locals retrenched, about 4,000 of them were PMETs.

sections.label: Job functions, skillsets, training programmes
sections.summary: It states there are 91 job functions, 291 job skillsets and more than 1,000 training programmes available to pursue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: In here, they can see very clearly there are altogether 91 job functions they can apply for.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: And if they want to apply for any one of these 91 job functions, there are 291 job skillsets they can pursue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: If they want to pursue any of those skillsets, there are more than 1,000 training programmes, all laid out in place for them to pursue.

sections.label: Ageing population and local employment
sections.summary: It states that with ageing and falling birth rates, local employment will peak and stop growing after 10 years, so better jobs matter more than more jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: With the trends of an ageing population and falling birth rates continuing, local employment will peak and stop growing after 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: This will do more harm than good to our country and people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Hence, the challenge we face in terms of job creation is no longer the more jobs the better, but the more the better jobs, the better.

sections.label: Retrenchment and layoff figures
sections.summary: It states last year's local resident retrenchments and layoffs were 71% of the total, and expects record retrenchments this year with PMETs about 70%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: As we know, last year's record number of local resident retrenchment and layoff made up 71% of the total.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: This year, I expect another round of record retrenchments and also PMETs would form the bulk, at least about 70% for those laid off.

sections.label: Removal from watch-list
sections.summary: It states that for one-fifth of companies, on TAFEP's recommendation, they were removed from the watch-list as their HR practices now match industry standard.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: For this one-fifth of companies, on the recommendation of TAFEP, we have decided to remove them from the watch-list because their HR practices are now on par with the industry standard.

sections.label: Companies on watch-list
sections.summary: It states that adding 180 and 80% of 100 gives about 250 companies on the watch-list.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: If we put 180 plus the 80% of the 100, we now have altogether about 250 companies on our watch-list.

sections.label: Expanding PCP programmes
sections.summary: It states that PCP is being expanded from 22 programmes to at least 50 by the end of this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Earlier, I talked about expanding PCP from 22 programmes to at least 50 by the end of this year.

sections.label: Hotel sector PMET vacancies
sections.summary: In the hotel sector, there are 2,000 vacancies, and 40% or 800 of them are PMET jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: For example, in the hotel sector, they have 2,000 vacancies, and 40% or 800 of them, are PMET jobs.

sections.label: EP scheme and retrenchment incentives
sections.summary: The question asks whether the EP scheme will be adjusted to consider Singaporeans first and whether incentives will be given to retain Singaporeans over EP holders during retrenchment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: First, will the Minister adjust the Employment Pass (EP) scheme such that Singaporeans with the necessary skills and experience are provided with the opportunities to be considered first for vacancies?

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Second, will the Minister consider providing incentives to employers to retain Singaporeans over EP holders during a retrenchment exercise, for example, widening the Career Support Programme so that employers can access them to keep Singaporeans employed, rather than wait for them to be retrenched, that is, keep them employed as they restructure their businesses?

sections.label: Tightening EP criteria
sections.summary: The EP criteria are being tightened to maximise complementarity between EP and locals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: What we are doing is to tighten the EP criteria to maximise the complementarity between EP and the locals.

sections.label: PCP wage and training subsidy
sections.summary: Under the PCP, wages and training programmes are subsidised during a retraining period of up to 18 to 24 months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Under the PCP, during the retraining period of up to a maximum of 18 to 24 months, we subsidise their wages and training programme.

sections.label: CSP wage subsidy for PMETs
sections.summary: Under the CSP, wages are subsidised for the first year for a PMET earning between $4,000 and $7,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: For example, if a PMET is earning between $4,000 and $7,000, under the CSP, we subsidise their wages for the first year.

sections.label: Helping mid-career PMETs
sections.summary: Priority in helping mid-career PMETs is through P-Max, which matches PMETs to SMEs, and private placement companies are being tried.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: In professional conversion, the last thing we want to do is to see a person giving up all the years of experience, expertise and skills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Therefore, our priority in helping the mid-career PMETs is through P-Max, which helps to match PMETs to the SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: P-Max is our way to help the SMEs to tap on the skills and experience of the mature PMETs and vice versa.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: On top of that, another area which we are now exploring is that for mature PMETs with many years of skills, experience and expertise, we think that the private placement companies may also be of great help to them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: We have started trying out the services of the private placement companies.
